Systems · 2026-11-13

Rethinking inference without NVLink

On our RTX 6000D cluster, two GPUs in the same server talk more slowly than two servers do. Every design choice in our stack follows from that one measurement.

40.6 → 5.9µs, one-row all-reduce
47%of a prefill chunk was pure communication
36 → 10.9ms per token, GLM-5.3 single stream

Long context · 2026-11-13

Making a million tokens usable

A million-token context is a capacity, communication and scheduling problem before it is a model feature. We do the KV accounting first, then take each model apart.

1,045,368input tokens, three needles retrieved

Deployment · 2026-11-13

Finding the useful throughput frontier

A faster batch is useful only while every user still gets an acceptable stream. We measured Kimi-K3 on eleven hardware configurations and drew the line at 40 tok/s per user.

1,991tok/s total, 41 tok/s per user, 2×B200

Agent reliability · 2026-11-13

Correctness beyond a successful response

An HTTP 200 and valid JSON are not enough. Agent workloads need complete streams, correct tool arguments and faithful protocol behavior, so every fix here comes with a controlled comparison.

4.7% → 0tool-argument leaks in long multi-turn sessions

Serving · 2026-11-13

A cache hit is not the end of the journey

Our cache hit rate was 98.6%, yet the first token still took 3.6 seconds. Following the bytes showed where the time went, and why a hit-rate dashboard can mislead.

98.6%cache hit rate, 3.6 s first token

Every iteration should leave better evidence

Recursive self-improvement, the way we mean it: not a model changing its own weights, but a team of people, agents and a shared knowledge base that gets better at getting better.
